current_row.boundary_rationale: Yahweh's own word-event formula opens the response to the burning, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ אַחֲרֵ֣י שְׂרֹ֣ף הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.36.27, byte), matching “Then Yahweh's word came to Jeremiah, after the king had burned” (web:Jer.36.27) A paseq falls at this same verse. The command to rewrite follows without a break (web:Jer.36.28), and a pronouncement naming Jehoiakim specifically opens on its own koh-amar, וְעַל יְהוֹיָקִ֤ים מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ תֹּאמַ֔ר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.36.29, byte), matching “Concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say, 'Yahweh says: "You” (web:Jer.36.29) charging him with burning the very scroll that warned of Babylon's coming -- a setumah falls at this same opening verse. A second koh-amar carries the sentence itself, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עַל יְהֽוֹיָקִים֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה לֹא יִֽהְיֶה לּ֥וֹ יוֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֑ד (oshb:Jer.36.30, byte), matching “Therefore Yahweh says concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: "He will have no one to sit on David's throne.” (web:Jer.36.30) -- no heir on David's throne, his own body cast out. The punishment then extends to his offspring, his servants, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem and Judah, closing on their own failure to listen (וּפָקַדְתִּ֨י עָלָ֧יו וְעַל זַרְע֛וֹ וְעַל עֲבָדָ֖יו אֶת עֲוֺנָ֑ם וְהֵבֵאתִ֣י עֲ֠לֵיהֶם וְעַל יֹשְׁבֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם וְאֶל אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֵ֧ת כָּל הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א שָׁמֵֽעוּ (oshb:Jer.36.31, byte), matching “I will punish him, his offspring, and his servants for their iniquity. I will bring on them, on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and on the men of Judah, all the evil that I have pronounced against them, but they didn't listen.” (web:Jer.36.31)); a setumah falls at this closing verse too. The chapter and the row close on Jeremiah's own replacement of the scroll, וְיִרְמְיָ֜הוּ לָקַ֣ח מְגִלָּ֣ה אַחֶ֗רֶת וַֽיִּתְּנָהּ֮ אֶל בָּר֣וּךְ בֶּן נֵרִיָּהוּ֮ הַסֹּפֵר֒ וַיִּכְתֹּ֤ב עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ מִפִּ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.36.32, byte), matching “Then Jeremiah took another scroll, and gave it to Baruch the scribe, the son of Neriah, who wrote therein from the mouth of Jeremiah” (web:Jer.36.32) continuing, וְע֨וֹד נוֹסַ֧ף עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם דְּבָרִ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים כָּהֵֽמָּה (oshb:Jer.36.32, byte), matching “and many similar words were added to them.” (web:Jer.36.32) A further setumah closes this same verse.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the specific sentence against Jehoiakim (verses 29 through 31) away from the general rewrite command (verses 27 and 28) into two rows was considered, since the second half narrows to name the king specifically, but rejected because the formula וְעַל יְהוֹיָקִ֤ים מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ תֹּאמַ֔ר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.36.29, byte) and the sentence's own formula, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.36.30, byte), both stand inside the same divine instruction to Jeremiah, so the mouth carrying the formula stays the same across that seam.
current_row.literature_type_guess: Yahweh's rewrite command, the sentence on Jehoiakim by name, and the scroll's replacement

current_row.boundary_rationale: The span opens the part on a reign-change notice, וַיִּ֨מְלָךְ מֶ֔לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בֶּן יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ תַּ֗חַת כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן יְה֣וֹיָקִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִמְלִ֛יךְ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte), matching “Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned as king instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.” (web:Jer.37.1) — the bytes name the new king’s predecessor כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ (Konyahu, byte; oshb:Jer.37.1), the Coniah form, one of three name forms this king carries across the book (sweep: 3 verses); the reign's installer carries no further identification beyond the royal title, “whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king” (web:Jer.37.1), the resh-family spelling נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר standing in the same clause (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte). Verse 2 continues the same notice with a general character report, וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֛ע ה֥וּא וַעֲבָדָ֖יו וְעַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא (oshb:Jer.37.2, byte), matching “But neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land, listened to Yahweh's words, which he spoke by the prophet Jeremiah.” (web:Jer.37.2) — naming the king, his servants, and the people of the land together, a summary claim about the reign rather than a dated scene. The inventory’s own setumah sits at oshb:Jer.36.32 (single-witness WLC archival, weak, tier-3 corroboration, governed by the Prophets addendum), immediately before this span’s own front seam; no mark falls inside verses 1-2 themselves.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding these two verses into the embassy scene that follows as one larger opening unit was rejected because verses 1-2 report the reign and a general hearing failure as a summary notice, while verse 3 turns to the narrated sending of named envoys carrying a specific request, וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ (oshb:Jer.37.3, byte).
current_row.literature_type_guess: regnal succession notice with a summary disobedience report
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: The clause naming Zedekiah's accession is itself the seam the part opens on, a reign change standing in for a dated formula at the head of a new narrative stretch. The predecessor's name appears here in its Coniah form; the book's other two forms for the same king, Jehoiachin and Jeconiah, belong to other chapters and are not engaged by this span. Nebuchadnezzar's resh-family spelling recurs through the chapters ahead (sweep: 29 verses), with a plene byform at Jer.49.28; the book also carries a nun-family spelling elsewhere (sweep: 6 verses), including a vav-less defective form at Jer.28.11 and Jer.28.14, none attested in this span.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The scene turns to Jeremiah's own movement once the siege lifts, וְהָיָ֗ה בְּהֵֽעָלוֹת֙ חֵ֣יל הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים מֵעַ֖ל יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם מִפְּנֵ֖י חֵ֥יל פַּרְעֹֽה (oshb:Jer.37.11, byte), matching “When the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh's army,” (web:Jer.37.11); a setumah marks this same verse in the inventory (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration), texture at the turn rather than its warrant. He is seized at Benjamin's gate on a charge of desertion and brought before the officials, matching “When he was in Benjamin's gate, a captain of the guard was there, whose name was Irijah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah; and he seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "You are defecting to the Chaldeans!"” (web:Jer.37.13); the officials strike him and hold him in Jonathan the scribe's house, matching “The princes were angry with Jeremiah, and struck him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe; for they had made that the prison.” (web:Jer.37.15). A petuchah closes the span at oshb:Jer.37.16 (single-witness WLC attestation, weak, tier-3 corroboration), כִּ֣י בָ֧א יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ אֶל בֵּ֥ית הַבּ֖וֹר וְאֶל הַֽחֲנֻ֑יוֹת וַיֵּֽשֶׁב שָׁ֥ם יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים (oshb:Jer.37.16, byte), where Jeremiah is reported to have remained many days.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the seizure at the gate from the imprisonment that follows into two rows was rejected because no formula, addressee change, or dated notice interrupts the single chain from seizure to the many days in the cells.
current_row.literature_type_guess: departure, seizure, and initial imprisonment narrative
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: The captain who seizes Jeremiah is identified by a three-generation line ending in a Hananiah, בֶּן חֲנַנְיָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.37.13, byte); this is Irijah's grandfather, a different bearer of the name from the prophet of chapter 28. Jonathan the scribe is named as the owner of the house turned prison, a detail the plea in the following span returns to by name.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A setumah closes the rescue span at oshb:Jer.38.13 (single-witness WLC evidence, weak, tier-3 corroboration) immediately before the king reopens contact on his own initiative, וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֗הוּ וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֤הוּ הַנָּבִיא֙ אֵלָ֔יו אֶל מָבוֹא֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ שֹׁאֵ֨ל אֲנִ֤י אֹֽתְךָ֙ דָּבָ֔ר אַל תְּכַחֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נִּי דָּבָֽר (oshb:Jer.38.14, byte), matching “Then Zedekiah the king sent and took Jeremiah the prophet to himself into the third entry that is in Yahweh’s house. Then the king said to Jeremiah,” (web:Jer.38.14) — a new location, the temple's third entry, and a demand that Jeremiah hide nothing from him. Jeremiah's wary reply opens verse 15; the king's sworn oath follows, and a further setumah is marked at that same verse, oshb:Jer.38.16 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration). Jeremiah's conditional oracle then answers in Yahweh's name, matching “Yahweh, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says:” (web:Jer.38.17) — promising Zedekiah's life and the city's safety if he surrenders to Babylon's princes, and the city's burning and his own capture if he refuses (continuing through web:Jer.38.18); a third setumah is marked at oshb:Jer.38.18 (single-witness WLC attestation, weak, tier-3 corroboration). Zedekiah's fear of the defectors closes that exchange, matching “I am afraid of the Jews who have defected to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hand, and they mock me.” (web:Jer.38.19) — a petuchah is marked at this same verse, oshb:Jer.38.19 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration) — and Jeremiah's reassurance in verse 20 answers that same fear without a further addressee change, the last speech introduction before what follows standing at וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.20, byte). Jeremiah continues at once into a further disclosure, וְאִם מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לָצֵ֑את זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִרְאַ֖נִי יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.38.21, byte), matching “But if you refuse to go out, this is the word that Yahweh has shown me:” (web:Jer.38.21) — the protasis carrying no speech introduction, no vocative, no addressee change, and no dated notice, and continuing the same conditional series already running at אִם יָצֹ֨א תֵצֵ֜א (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte) and וְאִ֣ם לֹֽא תֵצֵ֗א (oshb:Jer.38.18, byte). The women's taunt follows, matching “Behold, all the women who are left in the king of Judah’s house will be brought out to the king of Babylon’s princes, and those women will say,” (web:Jer.38.22), continuing in the same second-person address to Zedekiah that runs unbroken from verse 20 through the span's own close. A petuchah closes the span at oshb:Jer.38.23 (single-witness WLC record, weak, tier-3 corroboration), וְאֶת כָּל נָשֶׁ֣יךָ וְאֶת בָּנֶ֗יךָ מֽוֹצִאִים֙ אֶל הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וְאַתָּ֖ה לֹא תִמָּלֵ֣ט מִיָּדָ֑ם כִּ֣י בְיַ֤ד מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֙ תִּתָּפֵ֔שׂ וְאֶת הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את תִּשְׂרֹ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ (oshb:Jer.38.23, byte), where the wives and children are named alongside the city's burning, closing Jeremiah's own single unbroken turn opened at verse 20. The next participant change carrying its own speech introduction stands at וַיֹּ֨אמֶר צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.24, byte), matching “Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah,” (web:Jer.38.24) — where the following row already begins.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at Jer.38.21, where Jeremiah turns from direct counsel to a further disclosure introduced by a showing-formula, was considered, since that formula might seem to open its own report; but it is rejected because MT 38:21 carries no addressee change, no vocative, no narrative frame, and no dated notice — the last speech introduction stands one verse earlier at וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.20, byte), and the second-person address to the king continues unbroken through oshb:Jer.38.22 and oshb:Jer.38.23. The showing verb itself stands verse-medially at 38:21 rather than opening the verse, and (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, oshb:Jer.24.1 and oshb:Jer.38.21) is embedded inside Jeremiah's own ongoing address rather than standing as a separate report. A conditional series on the same exit-verb, אִם יָצֹ֨א תֵצֵ֜א (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte), וְאִ֣ם לֹֽא תֵצֵ֗א (oshb:Jer.38.18, byte), and the protasis of oshb:Jer.38.21 itself, runs across the very point any cut would fall, arguing continuity rather than division.
